subject: Reserved capacity term: phasing & GPU-price safeguard proposal
messages:
From: Derek White <derek.white@nimbus.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: Reserved capacity ask + GPU indexation question

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for walking us through Redwood's Dedicated offering yesterday. Nimbus is preparing a procurement request for a reserved capacity commitment to support our inference workloads (primarily chat and embeddings for our clinical product).

Initial ask from procurement: 36-month reserved commitment, 120 A100-equivalent GPU-months per month (we can map to your SKUs during contracting).

Key concern: recent GPU price volatility. Our procurement team wants either:
- an indexation clause that adjusts price if market GPU spot/list prices move >20% over a quarter, or
- an alternative: a price-safeguard mechanism (escrow/holdback) tied to a vendor-reported GPU price index.

Attached is our RFP extract and a short template of the indexation language. Can Redwood accomodate either approach, and, if so, what approval or finance review is needed on your side?

Appreciate a quick note on what flexibility we can expect and any tradeoffs to discount levels or tenor.

Best,
Derek White
Head of Procurement
Nimbus AI
[attachment: Nimbus_RFP_reserved_draft.pdf]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Derek White <derek.white@nimbus.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-05T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + GPU indexation question

Derek — thanks, and really good context. Short answer: yes, we can structure protection against GPU-market swings, but there are standard ways we've seen work better operationally.

Two practical options we typically propose:
1) Phased commitment + committed discount tiers: start with a 24-month core commitment and an optional 12-month tail you can elect (total 36). Discount depth tied to committed GPU-months; smaller frontload = slightly lower initial discount but faster procurement sign-off.

2) Price-safeguard with defined trigger bands: e.g., if a Redwood-verified GPU index moves up >25% quarter-over-quarter, Nimbus can elect a relief path (short-term credits or reduced billing rate for the affected months). To avoid excessive complexity, we recommend a cap (e.g., relief limited to first 15% of movement) plus an escrow mechanism to smooth reconciliation.

Tradeoffs: indexation increases contract complexity and requires finance/legal approvals on both sides. Longer tenors and higher upfront commit get better unit pricing (deeper discounts) and reduce the operational need for an indexation clause.

I looped in Laura (Finance) and Karthik (Product) to map approvals and capacity planning. Marcus — can you run a quick 3-scenario sensitivity (nominal / +25% GPU cost / +50% GPU cost) on the attached pricing_model_v2.xlsx and return a short note on whether our Dedicated fleet can absorb a short-term spike without requiring reallocation?

We can turn this into a mutual action plan (MAP) if Nimbus wants to proceed — include milestone: procurement sign, technical onboarding, first 90-day usage review.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[attachment: pricing_model_v2.xlsx]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-06T08:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity ask + GPU indexation question

Aditya — looping in finance POV. High level: we prefer avoiding open-ended indexation. If there is a protection mechanism, it should be structured as:
- Defined trigger windows and thresholds (clear math)
- Maximum relief cap as % of monthly bill
- Reconciliation via quarterly true-up (not retrospective multi-year adjustments)
- Escrow/holdback only up to X% (we need to confirm X; 5–12% range is common)

Karthik/Marcus: please provide the capacity impact note and an expected approval path/timeframe if Nimbus asks for a 25% relief cap and a 10% escrow. Finance will need modeled cashflow impact by month for the first 12 months.

Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-06T14:21:00Z
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity ask + GPU indexation question — sensitivity outputs

On Tue, Jul 06, 2026 at 08:45, laura_bennett@redwood.ai wrote:
> Aditya — looping in finance POV. High level: we prefer avoiding open-ended indexation. If there is a protection mechanism, it should be structured as...

Attached is a short CSV with three scenarios (nominal, +25%, +50%). Summary:
- Nominal: fleet utilization stays within planned buckets; no reassignments required for first 6 months.
- +25% GPU cost (transient, same utilization): unit margin reduces ~11% on committed units; we can absorb for 2–3 months without reallocating Dedicated capacity, but true-up/escrow reconciliation required to maintain margin targets.
- +50% GPU cost: requires either passing through some cost or accelerating migration of non-committed workloads to Best-Effort pools after month 3.

Conclusion: we can support a relief cap up to ~15% for transient shocks without operational churn. Anything beyond that needs a contractual pass-through or rebalancing triggers.

Attached: finance-sensitivity-run.csv
Marcus Lin
Sr. Infra Planner, Redwood Inference

From: Derek White <derek.white@nimbus.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: purchasing@nimbus.ai
Date: 2026-07-07T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + GPU indexation question

Aditya — thanks for the quick analysis and thanks Marcus/Laura for the sensitivity. Nimbus feedback from procurement:

We are willing to shift to a 24-month firm commitment + optional 12-month extension (auto-elect by month 18) to get pricing closer to your core discounts. For the price-safeguard, we propose:
- Trigger: Redwood index >25% QoQ
- Relief: up to 15% billing credit for triggered months
- Escrow: 10% holdback on monthly invoices, reconciled quarterly via true-up; unclaimed holdback returns to Redwood after 12 months

Procurement is OK with limited complexity if legal templates are clear. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the above structure (we need an exec-level sign-off pathway and a timeline for legal to review). If acceptable, we'll issue a redline-ready SOW and DocuSign envelope next week.

Derek
Derek White
Head of Procurement, Nimbus AI
